_note: House positions — Simply Enak's stated opinions. Hand-maintained (NOT a Payload snapshot; auto-sync does not touch this file). Agents MUST read this before drafting content: use registered stances; new stances require Maarten's sign-off (status: confirmed) before use. Entries are topic-scoped one-liners with sources so conviction is reused, never invented.

schema.topic: what this position is about (dish, place, practice)

positions.stance: Raja Kunyit (Musang King) is our favourite.
positions.why: Pauline's direct experience eating durian across Penang — Raja Kunyit consistently delivers the bittersweet depth and creamy texture we look for; it's the benchmark other cultivars are measured against.

positions.stance: June to July is the best time to find and eat durian.
positions.why: Main Penang harvest window aligns with southwest monsoon tail; fruit quality peaks when rainfall drops after the heavy May–June flush. Off-season fruit exists but is often from different states with longer transit.

positions.stance: The hills behind Balik Pulau produce some of the best durian in Malaysia, including the rare Black Thorn variety.
positions.why: Balik Pulau's microclimate (coastal breeze + elevation 100–300m) and older orchard stock — many trees 30+ years — yield fruit with intensity that lowland commercial plantings don't match. Black Thorn is almost exclusively from this pocket.

positions.topic: brand point of view on Malaysia
positions.stance: The Malaysia most tourists never see is the one worth showing.
positions.why: Our tours operate in residential neighbourhoods, wet markets, and home kitchens — places guidebooks skip. The conviction comes from 8 years of guests saying 'I never would've found this' about a stall 200m from their hotel.

positions.stance: Stall owners appreciate being asked what is vegetarian.
positions.why: Repeated observation on tours: when guests ask 'what's vegetarian?' the aunty pauses, thinks, then offers 2–3 off-menu adaptations (skip the ikan bilis, swap belacan for taucu). Silence means default pork-lard base; asking unlocks the real options.

positions.stance: Temple canteens are worth seeking out; the food and atmosphere beat the regular tourist trail.
positions.why: Non-commercial kitchens cooking for devotees, not turnover. Vegetarian by default, generous portions, RM3–6 per plate. The atmosphere — communal tables, zero performative service — is the antithesis of tourist-zone dining. We've taken 200+ guests; zero complaints.

positions.topic: herb and spice sourcing in KL
positions.stance: Best selection of fresh herbs and whole spices is at KL wet markets plus Indian grocers in Brickfields and Little India.
positions.why: Wet market vendors (Chow Kit, Pudu) restock daily from Cameron Highlands and Thai border — herbs harvested <24h ago. Brickfields/Little India grocers carry whole spices (star anise, clove, cardamom) in bulk turnover that supermarket jars can't match for aroma.

positions.stance: Red bean soup, peanut paste soup, and black-eyed pea soup are our tong sui picks.
positions.why: These three represent the texture spectrum we value: red bean (whole beans, skin-on, earthy), peanut paste (velvety, nut-oil richness), black-eyed pea (delicate, slightly floral). Cendol and ABC are ubiquitous; these three reward seeking out.

positions.stance: Craft souvenirs are a little pricey, worth it for the craftsmanship.
positions.why: Batik block-printing, songket weaving, and pewter in KL workshops employ heritage techniques with living artisans. RM150–400 buys an object with documented provenance; mass-market souvenirs (RM20–50) are factory-printed with no maker traceability. The price gap is the craftsmanship gap.

positions.stance: Pulau Ketam from a Port Klang stopover is a schlep, but worth it in our opinion.
positions.why: 45 min ferry each way + 20 min KTM from KL Sentral + walking the stilt village = 4–5 hours round trip. The payoff: mangrove-boardwalk silence, fresh steamed fish at floating restaurants (RM35–50), and zero tour buses. Only worth it if you have 6+ hours in KL and value quiet over efficiency.

positions.topic: brand point of view on street food experience
positions.stance: Experience street food with someone who knows the stalls and which aunty makes the best roti canai.
positions.why: Our guides have eaten at these stalls weekly for years — they know which aunty's dough rests 4 hours vs 30 minutes, which stall switches oil at noon. That knowledge difference is the product; the food is the vehicle. Guests who DIY the same route miss the 'why this stall' layer entirely.
